content.comment_body: Thank you [user_name]! I've completed the backup successfully. I'm planning to purchase a new [product_name] to replace the discontinued [product_name] ([article_no]). Can anyone confirm which model is compatible with [product_name] [article_no]? Best regards, [user_name].
The current [product_name] replacement is [article_no]. For this model, you'll need the updated software [product_name] V[version_no].

Hello, These two types are not compatible. Expansion modules from your previous [product_name] cannot be connected to the new [product_name], and memory or battery cards are not transferable. If you only use a [product_name] basis module, compatibility will not be an issue. Note: If you order a [product_name] basis module now, it will come in V[version_no]. You'll need [product_name] V[version_no] to program it.
The basis modules themselves are compatible, but expansion modules are not. Since the user didn't mention expansion modules, there shouldn't be any problem.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are discussing the replacement of a discontinued [product_name] ([article_no]) with a compatible [product_name] basis module. The key focus is compatibility between old and new modules, especially regarding expansion modules and programming software versions. It is clarified that basic modules can be replaced directly, but older expansion modules and memory cards cannot be reused, and the latest programming software is necessary for the new module.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a simple, compatible replacement for a discontinued [product_name], ideally one that works with existing hardware and can be programmed without extra difficulties.
